risk_if_not_implemented: Without Stateful Hash-Based Signatures for Firmware & Code Signing, embedded and IoT technologies may operate with unknown, insecure or unmonitored configurations, creating exploitable footholds. Based on the risk and threat mapping for this control, this deficiency most likely exposes the organization to Unauthorized Modification / Loss of System Integrity (R-AM-2), Long-Term Confidentiality Loss from Cryptographic Obsolescence (R-IP-1), Loss of Authenticity / Provenance (R-IP-5), and most likely increases susceptibility to Human Error (MT-9), Harvest Now / Decrypt Later (HNDL) (MT-28), Cryptographic Compromise / Cryptanalytic Capability Advancement (MT-31).

compensating_control_1.name: Public Key Infrastructure (PKI)
compensating_control_1.description: Mechanisms exist to securely implement an internal Public Key Infrastructure (PKI) infrastructure or obtain PKI services from a reputable PKI service provider.
compensating_control_1.justification: Public Key Infrastructure (PKI) (CRY-09) provides cryptographic protection and key governance that compensates for the absence of Stateful Hash-Based Signatures for Firmware & Code Signing (QTS-09.2) by ensuring data confidentiality and integrity through alternative or complementary cryptographic mechanisms. Given the technology-focused nature of this control, this compensating control targets the same underlying risk objective through an alternative approach, helping to maintain an acceptable level of residual risk until the primary control can be implemented.

compensating_control_2.name: Integrity Assurance & Enforcement (IAE)
compensating_control_2.description:
Automated mechanisms exist to:
(1) Identify unauthorized deviations from an approved secure baseline configuration; and
(2) Implement automated resiliency actions to remediate the unauthorized change.
compensating_control_2.justification: Integrity Assurance & Enforcement (IAE) (CFG-08.2) provides configuration and supply-chain hardening that compensates for the absence of Stateful Hash-Based Signatures for Firmware & Code Signing (QTS-09.2) by enforcing secure settings and trusted software sources to reduce inherent exposure. Given the technology-focused nature of this control, this compensating control targets the same underlying risk objective through an alternative approach, helping to maintain an acceptable level of residual risk until the primary control can be implemented.
